chunks: And by this chain, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ḥammād ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, from Muʿādh, the صاحب of the cloaks, who said:
I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying:
Indeed, Allah did not ask His creatures for a loan from what is in their hands out of any need on His part for that; and whatever right belongs to Allah, it is only for His Guardian.

key_terms.إِنَّ اللَّهَ: Indeed Allah; an affirmation of Allah’s absolute reality and independence
key_terms.حَقٍّ: A right; a due or entitlement established by Allah
key_terms.خَلْقَهُ: His creation; the human beings addressed with obligations
key_terms.قَرْضًا: A loan; giving wealth in the manner described as lending to Allah
key_terms.لِوَلِيِّهِ: For His Guardian; for the one vested with divine authority and guardianship

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah ask people to give if He has no need of them?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that Allah is absolutely free of need and does not command financial giving because of any deficiency or dependence. It also states that the rights attributed to Allah in this matter are realized through His wali, indicating the authority and due of the divinely appointed Imam عليه السلام.
